articles.title: Stock market outlook: RBI rate decision, earnings, oil & more, here's what will drive D-street this week
articles.summary: Indian stock markets are set for another potentially volatile week, with a mix of domestic and global factors likely to determine the direction of
articles.body: Indian stock markets are set for another potentially volatile week, with a mix of domestic and global factors likely to determine the direction of equities. The Reserve Bank of India’s interest rate decision, the start of the corporate earnings season, crude oil prices and global bond yields are among the key triggers investors will track.The RBI’s monetary policy decision will be the principal domestic event. Investors will look for signals on the central bank’s policy stance, inflation outlook and growth projections, which could offer cues on the trajectory of domestic interest rates and financial markets.“The RBI’s policy decision will be the principal domestic trigger. The US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes will subsequently offer insights into the extent of support among US policymakers for further monetary tightening beyond the September rate increase,” Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a Research Analyst firm, said, as quoted by PTI.The week will also mark the beginning of the September-quarter earnings season, with IT major TCS scheduled to announce its results on October 8. Retail major DMart will also be among the key companies reporting their earnings.“RBI's monetary policy meeting will be closely watched. The policy stance, inflation outlook and growth projections will provide important cues on the near-term trajectory of domestic interest rates and financial markets,” Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking, said.On the macroeconomic front, India’s final HSBC Services PMI and Composite PMI readings for September are due on October 6. Foreign institutional investors’ trading activity will also remain an important factor for the market.Crude oil prices are another major concern, particularly with Brent crude trading above USD 100 a barrel. Elevated oil prices could add to pressure on India’s external balances and inflation outlook, while continued geopolitical uncertainty could keep the risk premium in energy prices high.“Crude oil remains the most immediate macroeconomic concern. Brent crude trading above USD 100 a barrel continues to intensify pressure on India’s external balances and inflation outlook, while persistent geopolitical uncertainty threatens to keep the risk premium in energy prices elevated,” Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, an online trading and wealth tech firm, said.Global bond yields will also be closely watched for their impact on risk appetite and foreign flows. A moderation in US Treasury yields could ease pressure on emerging-market assets, while a further rise could make US assets relatively more attractive and encourage continued portfolio reallocation away from emerging markets, Ponmudi said.The domestic market enters the week after ending lower for the eighth consecutive week, weighed down by foreign selling, rupee weakness, elevated crude prices and rising global bond yields.The Sensex lost 1,986.04 points, or 2.68 per cent, last week, while the Nifty declined 718.55 points, or 3.10 per cent. articles.title: Micron stock offers an important reminder for investors
articles.summary: Micron is a beast. Don't forget that.
articles.body:
I have a healthy obsession with Micron ( MU ) stock.

You probably got that vibe this week on my show, Sozzi Unleashed .

I can't find a single company in the expansive universe of stocks I follow that is growing by billions of dollars per quarter and trades on a laughable single-digit forward P/E ratio. (Thank you for the reminder on this one, Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace .)

How the stock market works has a lot in common with how overachievers view themselves.

The stock market is always in a race with itself to find the next big thing. Predict the next big thing, and the trading portfolio could look a lot greener. Overachievers are in the boat, always looking to execute on the next big thing in a bid to keep their overachiever status intact.

For both, it's a vicious cycle that often leads to one outcome: failing to appreciate the here and now.

I think this logic could be applied to Micron's financials.

Micron blew it out of the water on its earnings day this week. Crushed it on every single line item. And with guidance.

The main headline was that the memory chipmaker beat sales and profit forecasts for the quarter, driven by voracious demand from the AI boom . Guidance was also strong, except for margin comments on the earnings call — which may have caused the muted market reaction.

But keep Micron's quarter in the proper context.

Consider this: Micron added about $43 billion in sales during the most recent quarter compared to the year-ago quarter. It added more than $13 billion in sales from the quarter reported three months ago! All of this is massive.

Operating margins exploded in all business segments. In fact, operating margins are over 80% in some segments.

What's more, Micron execs signal tight capacity and higher prices for its products until 2028.

"We believe expectations for tightening supply-demand conditions through both 2027 and 2028 meaningfully extend the industry's runway for strong pricing and earnings growth, addressing a key investor concern that current fundamentals represent a cyclical peak," D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria said.

The stock market is forward-looking, so the race is on to predict Micron's next 12 months of results. Don't lose sight of what this company is doing right now, is all I'm saying.

The same goes for your overachieving self.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.
